blocks.md: Every bound derived so far, whether metric, learned, or temporal, assumes that the sensor behaves as calibrated: propagation bounds the error of a sensor working as modeled, not one that has stopped working that way while still delivering frames at its nominal rate. A navigation camera can fail in two ways that look entirely different to downstream software. If its serializer link loses lock, the driver raises an error and the frame never arrives.

questions.q: The section **Perception Failure Modes and Sensor Degradation** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Spatial error is spent from the same clearance as age, so the clearance inset rests on a measured high quantile of residuals against ground truth, which for stereo grows with range squared.

Detectable faults raise flags and age out honestly, while silent failures (saturation, contamination, fog backscatter, a misdated frame) deliver valid tensors, so the design must convert silent modes into detectable ones.

Observation age runs from the exposure midpoint to dispatch, accumulates stage by stage (exposure, readout, transport, DMA, ISP, backbone, dispatch), and is paid in blind travel that no later stage returns.

A measurement is dated at its exposure midpoint or per-point firing time, never at arrival, and rolling-shutter rows and LiDAR sweeps sample the scene at different instants that capture-time geometry must undo.
